questions.question: Explain why the Sun is called a star and why it is at the centre of the Solar System.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is a star because it is a huge, very hot ball of glowing gas that gives out its own light and heat. It looks bigger and brighter than other stars only because it is much closer to us. It is at the centre of the Solar System because its gravity pulls on the planets and keeps them moving around it in their orbits.

questions.question: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun, and explain the difference between the inner and outer planets.
questions.expected_answer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The four inner planets, Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, are fairly small and made of rock and metal, so they are rocky planets. The four outer planets, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, are huge and made mostly of gas, so they are gas giants.

questions.question: What is the asteroid belt and where is it found?
questions.expected_answer: The asteroid belt is a wide ring of millions of rocky and metal lumps called asteroids, which orbit the Sun. It lies between Mars and Jupiter. Some asteroids are as small as pebbles and others are hundreds of kilometres across; the biggest, Ceres, is also called a dwarf planet. The asteroids are very far apart from each other.
